title: ReGenHuman: Re-Generating Human Appearances for Realistic Full-Body Video Anonymization
claim: Prior methods yield unrealistic or inconsistent outputs and trade off key criteria; ours is realistic, consistent, and best across all axes.
layout: 2 panels: left video-frame grid by method, right scatter plot; red circles mark failures
description: The figure has two panels. The left panel is a film-strip grid of video frames. Rows are Input, DeepPrivacy2, FADM, Ours (StructHuman) and Ours (StructAll). Columns are two scenes, each with three frames: a woman on a purple set and men at an awards stage. Red ellipses and arrows on the baseline rows mark unrealistic humans and identity changes across frames. A green ellipse on the StructAll row marks the anonymized background text. The right panel is a scatter plot. Privacy (re-identification attack success, lower is better) is on the x-axis, reversed. Quality z-score is on the y-axis. Marker shape shows method family, and a viridis colorbar shows downstream VQA utility. A large green star labeled Ours sits in the top-right corner, and a gray arrow labeled 'better' points toward it. The eye goes first to the star and to the red circles.
caption: We propose \method, the first pipeline for realistic full-body video anonymization. Past methods for full-body anonymization such as DeepPrivacy2 [ref] and FADM [ref] are inadequate for video --- they either generate anatomically unrealistic humans or do not depict the same identity across frames. On the other hand, our ReGenHuman's generations are realistic and temporally consistent, with our StructAll generation being able to anonymize the background and accompanying text (left). We evaluate current anonymization approaches on privacy (Clothes-changing re-identification mAP on CCVID [ref] with CSCI [ref]), quality (z-score across metrics from VBench 1 and 2 [ref]), and utility (zero-shot video question answering accuracy on HOI-Gen1M [ref]). Our approach achieves the best tradeoff of all prior baselines, setting a new standard in video anonymization (right).
abstract: Anonymizing human-centric video data is an understudied problem. Prior anonymization techniques either blur or redact pixels at the cost of realism and downstream utility, or generate frame-by-frame at the cost of temporal coherence. We introduce ReGenHuman, the first full-body video anonymization pipeline that is simultaneously realistic, temporally consistent, and anonymous by construction. Contrary to past approaches which redact or edit the inputs directly, we propose a regenerate, don't edit paradigm. Our approach composites 2D pose, segmentation, and monocular depth into two complementary conditioning streams - StructAll and StructHuman, which are used to fine-tune a video-to-video diffusion backbone on in-the-wild human videos, synthesizing the human regions entirely from identity-free structural cues. We evaluate our model on privacy, quality, and utility, and show that our ReGenHuman achieves the best tradeoff across all three axes against current baselines. We further show that our anonymized videos remain effective for downstream tasks, including video question answering.
